sentences.asr: As the graph shows, China's urbanization rate rose from 19.39% in 1980 to 60.6% in 2019.
The increase was especially rapid between 1995 and 2010, when the rate jumped from 29.04% to 49.95%.
In 2011, it reached 51.27%, passing the 50% mark, meaning that for the first time more Chinese people lived in urban areas than in rural areas.
The rate continued to rise after that, though at a slower pace.
This remarkable progress reflects China's great achievements in urbanization.
Hundreds of millions of people have moved from the countryside to cities, where they enjoy better jobs, education and medical care.
Modern infrastructure, such as subways, high-speed railways and new residential areas, has transformed the appearance of cities and greatly improved people's quality of life.
Urbanization has also served as a powerful engine of economic growth, creating a huge domestic market and countless new business opportunities.
Of course, rapid urbanization has also brought challenges, such as traffic congestion and high housing costs.
Looking ahead, China should pursue people-centered urbanization, making cities greener and more livable while narrowing the gap between urban and rural areas.
Only then will the achievements of urbanization truly benefit everyone.
